column1: • REFER to Ready Reckoner Charts for Antimicrobial Administration, Time gaps between the Loading
and Maintenance Dose
• Approved IV Push and IM administration, Food and Antimicrobial Interactions and
Dialysis adjustments
• Consult ID Pharmacist for drug/food interactions, dose optimization and dose adjustments as per
renal, hepatic impairment and obesity
• Consider TDM for Vancomycin, Azole Antifungals and Isoniazid and Rifampicin
• Maintain appropriate records of Antimicrobial duration
BLOOD STREAM
• Send blood cultures and then start antibiotics
• Use loading dose in sepsis/septic shock regardless of renal dysfunction
• Prolong beta lactam infusion in sepsis/septic shock or critically ill patients
• Do not treat positive central venous catheter tip cultures without BSI if source control is achieved
• Avoid high lipophilic antibiotics in BSI (Eg. Tigecycline)
• Do not treat common blood culture contaminants (CoNS, Micrococcus, etc.) unless it is grown in
multiple cultures
• Avoid Amikacin for systemic infections with P. aeruginosa
• Use Minocycline 200 mg BD for CRAB as per new CLSI breakpoints
• Avoid Vancomycin, Teicoplanin for MSSA infections
URINARY TRACT
• Do not screen or treat for asymptomatic bacteriuria with antibiotics unless pregnant patient or
undergoing urological procedure
• Send urine samples from fresh catheters, not old ones
• Do not treat pyuria/bacteriuria from long-term catheters or intermittent self-catheterization
• Investigate MRSA in urine further- Check for systemic MRSA infection
RESPIRATORY
• Doxycycline/ Macrolides remain effective for CAP pathogens
• Stop antibiotics if viral etiology confirmed and no secondary bacterial infections
• Reserve Minocycline for MDR nosocomial infections
• Add anaerobic cover only for aspiration, lung abscess, or empyema
INTRA-ABDOMINAL
• Ensure adequate source control
• Shorter antibiotic courses suffice post source-control unless abscess is present
• Do not treat sterile necrotizing pancreatitis- only infected cases
• Aggressive hydration recommended in pancreatitis
CARDIOVASCULAR
• Day 1 of therapy = 1st day of negative blood culture
• Administer combination antibiotics close together for synergistic killing
• Use bactericidal regimen with good penetration
BONE & JOINT INFECTIONS
• Initial treatment should be with intravenous antibiotics
• Choose an antibiotic with good bone penetration and biofilm activity (if there is prosthesis)
• Avoid Vancomycin, Teicoplanin for MSSA infections
SURGICAL PROPHYLAXIS
• Stop prophylactic antibiotics within 24 hr in Clean and Clean contaminated surgeries
• Repeat intraoperative dose if surgery incision time exceeds >3 hr or blood loss > 1.5 litres
• Administer prophylactic prior to within 1 hr of incision: complete the dose 15 min before tourniquet
inflation and CPB circuit application where necessary
• Documenting incision and closure time and duration of surgery
MENINGITIS
• Lipophilic antibiotics penetrates rapidly in CSF. Hydrophilic antibiotics depend on inflammation
• Teicoplanin has delayed entry in CSF due to high protein binding
• CNS penetration is conveyed in the form of CSF-to-Serum ratio
• Bactericidal effect requires peak concentration exceeding 10-30x MBC
